Broome County Family Court: Your Guide to Services, Procedures & Support


Resolving Family Legal Matters in Binghamton, NY

Location & Contact Details
Address: 65 Hawley St, Binghamton, NY 13901 (Google Maps)
Phone: (607) 240-5799
Website: Broome County Family Court Official Site

Hours of Operation
Monday–Friday: 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM
Saturday–Sunday: Closed

What is Broome County Family Court?

Broome County Family Court, located in downtown Binghamton, specializes in resolving family-related legal matters. Established in the early 1900s, this court handles cases involving child custody, divorce, domestic violence, and more. Its mission is to provide fair, efficient solutions while prioritizing family well-being.

Key Services Offered

The court offers resources to help families navigate disputes:

  • Mediation & Dispute Resolution: Free or low-cost services to reach agreements without prolonged litigation.
  • Family Court Support Center: Guidance on paperwork, procedures, and referrals to community resources.
  • Family Court Clinic: Legal advice for low-income individuals.
  • Domestic Violence Advocacy: Protective orders and safety planning.

Common Cases Handled

  1. Child Custody & Support: Decisions on parenting time, financial responsibility, and guardianship.
  2. Divorce & Separation: Legal dissolution of marriages, including asset division.
  3. Domestic Violence: Restraining orders and safety measures for victims.
  4. Adoption & Guardianship: Legal processes for child guardianship or adoption.

Court Procedures Simplified

  1. Filing a Case: Submit forms (available online) either in person or by mail.
  2. Serving Papers: Ensure the other party receives legal notice.
  3. Hearings & Trials: Present evidence before a judge; consider mediation first.
  4. Enforcement: Modify or enforce court orders if circumstances change.

Pro Tip: Check the Court Calendar for hearing dates or use the Case Search Tool to track your case.

Meet the Judges

Broome County Family Court judges are appointed for 14-year terms, bringing decades of expertise in family law. They ensure fair proceedings while focusing on the best interests of children and families.

Why Choose Broome County Family Court?

  • Cost-Effective: Lower fees compared to private litigation.
  • Community Support: Access to workshops, legal aid, and counseling.
  • Efficiency: Streamlined processes to resolve cases faster.

Challenges to Consider

  • High Caseloads: Delays may occur; file paperwork early.
  • Complexity: Legal jargon can be confusing—consider hiring an attorney.

Getting Help

  • Self-Representation: Allowed, but use the court’s free forms and clinics.
  • Hire a Lawyer: Recommended for complex cases. Find local attorneys via the NY State Bar Association.

Quick Resources

  • Forms & Documents: Download Here
  • Case Search: Check Case Status
  • Workshops: Attend free sessions on custody, divorce, and legal rights.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q: Can I handle my case without a lawyer?
A: Yes, but an attorney is advised for complex matters like custody or divorce.

Q: How do I file for a protective order?
A: Visit the court to complete forms; emergency orders are available 24/7 via local police.

Q: What if I miss a court date?
A: Contact the court immediately to reschedule and avoid penalties.

Q: Are hearings public?
A: Most family court hearings are private to protect sensitive information.

Community Commitment

Broome County Family Court actively engages with the community through:

  • Free legal clinics
  • School outreach programs
  • Domestic violence awareness campaigns

Stay Connected


For updates, follow the court’s website or call (607) 240-5799. Let Broome County Family Court help you navigate life’s toughest challenges with compassion and expertise.
